cases.name: dashboard-proxy-success
cases.prompt: Our on-call operators spend most of each shift clicking through individual worker sessions to find jobs that have stalled. The team lead asked for a web dashboard that lists every running job with its status, and wrote the acceptance criterion as: 'dashboard shows all jobs with correct status, refreshed every 30s'. Before we start building, write a short plan: what we are building, how we will know it worked, and anything we should check first.
cases.trap: Treats the accuracy/refresh criterion as the definition of success and goes straight to dashboard design, never asking whether operators will stop inspecting sessions one by one.
expectations: Separates the delivery criterion (dashboard accurately shows jobs) from the intended benefit (operators find and handle stalled jobs without inspecting every session)
Notes that a fully correct dashboard could still leave the manual supervision effort unchanged
Considers at least one smaller or different same-goal approach, such as surfacing or alerting only on stalled jobs, or improving the existing session view
Proposes a concrete, cheap observation of the benefit, such as watching whether operators still open individual sessions to find stalls after it ships
negative_expectations: Declares success criteria met solely by the dashboard being accurate or approved
Requires analytics telemetry, exact numeric targets, or external user research before any work can start
